title: Regional quantization + batching: supply/demand proforma
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is a working proforma to reconcile regional GPU supply against forecasted inference demand under alternate quantization and batching profiles. Focus: estimate usable throughput, expected quality delta (relative to FP16 baseline), and utilization implications for US-WEST, US-EAST, EU, APAC for H100 / A100 / L4 class nodes. Not final — used for capacity commit guidance and Dedicated region sizing.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline model family: rwd-large-v2 (context 2048 tokens).
- FP16 baseline throughput measured on H100: 320 tokens/s per GPU single-thread for seq=64, batch=1.
- INT8 quantization yields ~1.7x throughput, 4-bit (Q4) yields ~2.6x throughput vs FP16 on H100 given optimized kernels and KV-cache behavior.
- Batch behavior: effective tokens/sec scales sublinearly with batch size due to latency tail and KV cache warmups. We use empirically measured scaling factors below.
- Quality delta: measured as % increase in token-level perplexity and application-level ROUGE/EM proxies. Values are workload dependent; we use conservative delta estimates.
- Price assumptions: cloud GPU hour list rates normalized (H100=12.0, A100-80GB=6.5, L4=1.2) normalized units used for relative cost proformas.

Scaling factors (empirical, per-GPU):
- Batch scaling (relative throughput vs batch=1): batch=1 -> 1.0, batch=4 -> 2.2, batch=8 -> 3.4, batch=16 -> 4.1 (diminishing returns).
- Quantization multipliers (H100): FP16=1.0, INT8=1.7, Q4=2.6. On A100 assume ~0.95x H100 multipliers; L4 optimized for small batches: multiplier ~1.8 at INT8, Q4 not recommended for largest models.

Summary table: region capacity and short-run proforma (per-GPU throughput token/s for seq=64, model=rwd-large-v2)

Region | GPU type | Count | FP16 b=1 | FP16 b=8 | INT8 b=8 | Q4 b=8 | est quality delta (INT8) | est quality delta (Q4)
-------|----------|-------|----------|---------|---------|--------|--------------------------|----------------------
US-WEST| H100     | 120   | 320      | 1088    | 1849    | 2810   | +1.8%                    | +3.4%               
US-EAST| A100-80  | 80    | 300      | 1020    | 1530    | 2340   | +2.2%                    | +3.9%               
EU     | H100     | 60    | 320      | 1088    | 1849    | 2810   | +1.9%                    | +3.5%               
APAC   | L4       | 200   | 48       | 163     | 293     | N/A    | +2.5%                    | N/A                 

Notes on table: FP16 b=8 = FP16 single-GPU throughput * batch scaling factor (3.4). INT8 and Q4 apply quant multipliers on FP16 b=8. L4 numbers measured on latency-optimized small batch traffic and scale poorly to Q4 for this model.

Projected demand slices (monthly avg tokens/day by region)
- Baseline (conservative growth): US-WEST 2.4B, US-EAST 1.1B, EU 0.9B, APAC 0.7B
- Peak day factor: 1.8x baseline

Per-region utilization proforma (month average):
Region | Provisioned GPUs | Effective tokens/day capacity (FP16 b=8) | Utilization @ baseline | Utilization @ INT8 b=8 (if rolled)
US-WEST | 120 | 120 * 1088 * 86.4k (sec/day) => 11.2B | 21% | 38%
US-EAST | 80  | 80 * 1020 * 86.4k => 7.05B | 16% | 25%
EU      | 60  | 60 * 1088 * 86.4k => 5.6B  | 16% | 28%
APAC    | 200 | 200 * 163 * 86.4k => 2.82B | 25% | 45%

Interpretation:
- Under FP16 (batch-optimized) we have significant headroom in US regions; APAC L4 fleet is smaller-per-GPU throughput and will hit utilization higher despite larger GPU count.
- Rolling to INT8 increases tokens/day capacity ~1.7x (per earlier multipliers) and reduces observed utilization, but introduces non-negligible quality drift.

Quality vs capacity tradeoff (qualitative):
- INT8: generally safe for generation tasks with conservative biasing and temperature tuning; expect small generative artifacts and ~2% proxy task metric reduction. Good candidate for background-heavy low-SLO routes or non-critical embeddings.
- Q4 (4-bit): larger throughput wins but visible regressions on rare-token generation and structured output; requires robust regression test-suite (prompt-set evals) before large rollouts.

Operational notes and guardrails for rollouts:
1) Canary profile: start with 5% traffic to INT8 on dedicated A/B canary model per region with routing policy that sends high-risk customer sessions to FP16 fallback.
2) Monitoring hooks: token-level perplexity delta, per-prompt-soft-fail rate (structured-output mismatch), per-route latency P50/P95/P99.
3) Automatic rollback triggers: +5% perplexity vs baseline on canary or +1% product metric drop over 24h.
4) Fallback policy: route to FP16 variant in same region or cross-region fallback to preserve latency SLOs (costly but reduces user impact).

Short financial proforma (relative units):
- Example: US-WEST H100 fleet hourly normalized cost: 120 * 12.0 = 1,440 units/hr.
- Cost per million tokens (FP16 b=8): approximate: cost_units_per_hr / tokens_per_hr. Tokens/hr for fleet = 120 * 1088 * 3600 = ~470M tokens/hr. Cost per million tokens = 1,440 / 470 = 3.06 units/M tokens.
- Under INT8 (tokens/hr *1.7 => ~799M tokens/hr) cost per M tokens = 1,440 / 799 = 1.80 units/M tokens.
- Conclusion: INT8 reduces unit cost ~41% at the fleet level but must be balanced against quality/regression risk for critical routes.

Sensitivity scenarios (quick):
1) 10% traffic growth month-on-month for 6 months -> US-WEST utilization under FP16 hits ~50% in month 4. INT8 pushes that out to month 7.
2) Model size increase (rwd-xxl) reduces per-GPU throughput by ~40% -> effective utilization jumps; need ~50% more GPUs or quant+batching to compensate.
3) Regional demand shift to APAC (x2) -> APAC L4 fleet becomes primary bottleneck; recommend mixed deployment of A100 spots or Dedicated H100 in APAC for latency-sensitive customers.

Recommended action items (next 60 days):
- Run controlled INT8 canaries in US-WEST and EU on 10 GPUs each, collect metric deltas on a 2000-prompt smoke-set (owner: Jamal).
- Expand production regression set for structured-output customers (owner: Priya).
- Build cost dashboard slice for tokens/M-unit by quant profile and route (owner: Li Wei).
- Evaluate APAC A100 spot pool feasibility for Q3 to relieve L4 pressure (owner: Tomás).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Acceptable quality delta thresholds per customer tier (PLG free tier vs enterprise SLA).
- Cross-region fallback SLOs and whether budget allows cross-region fallbacks for enterprise customers.
- Approval to run Q4 experiments on rwd-xxl in INT8; risk review required.

Appendix: quick measured micro-benchmarks (seq=64)
- H100 FP16 b=1: 320 t/s, b=8: 1088 t/s
- H100 INT8 b=8: 1849 t/s
- A100 FP16 b=1: 300 t/s, b=8: 1020 t/s; INT8 b=8: 1530 t/s
- L4 FP16 b=1: 48 t/s, b=8: 163 t/s; INT8 b=8: 293 t/s

Doc history / notes: working proforma derived from bench runs in /benchmarks/quant-batch-2025 and cost model v2.0. This sheet is intentionally conservative on quality delta numbers; finalize with applied-ml sign-off before Dedicated-wide rollouts.
